text:
Separating punishment from its justification matters because the same act of inflicting suffering can be defended on different grounds (retribution, deterrence, rehabilitation), and each ground sets different limits on who may be punished, how severely, and for how long. If the two are conflated, punishment appears justified simply by existing, and we lose the independent standard needed to criticize, limit, or reform it. So keeping them apart is what makes punishment open to moral and legal scrutiny.
